name: Caleb
bio:
Caleb is the son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah, one of only two of the twelve spies who brought back a faithful report. When Moses sent the leaders of the twelve tribes to spy out Canaan, ten of the spies returned with an exaggerated, discouraging report, frightening the people into retreat; Caleb, however, calmed the people before Moses, saying, "Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it" (Numbers 13:30).

Joshua and Caleb together tore their clothes and insisted before the whole congregation that the land of Canaan was exceedingly good, declaring, "If the LORD delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us... only rebel not ye against the LORD, neither fear ye the people of the land" (Numbers 14:6-9) — yet the congregation nearly stoned them both for it. God declared that because of the people's rebellion, that whole generation twenty years and older would not enter the promised land — except Caleb, who, because he "had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully," would enter the land he had spied out, and his descendants would possess it (Numbers 14:24). Caleb later saw this promise fulfilled in the book of Joshua, personally requesting and receiving Hebron as his inheritance at eighty-five years old, still claiming the strength of his youth for battle — a story told in Joshua 14.
